criteria.title: diag.bundle exports the stated fields, anonymised by default

checks.test: acceptance_diag::ac_28_bundle_exports_the_stated_fields
checks.assert: diag.bundle returns exactly the stated fields and no path, no remote URL and no email survives anonymisation by default.

Against a real index whose locations sit under a home directory, a bundle exported with the default setting carries no home directory, no drive letter, no mount root and no user name — only the basename and the per-volume pseudonym §11.4 specifies. The same export with SHOW REAL PATHS must put them back, so a clean default run is known to have had something to remove.
checks.reason: A reviewer performs this before a release, against the built binary rather than the source. It is not automated here for two reasons. The cargo half (AC-28-fields, owner 17) asserts the document's shape but builds no bundle from host-shaped paths, so it cannot see an anonymiser that stopped covering a field. And the control half is what makes the result mean anything: without re-exporting the same index with real paths and watching the assertion fail, a clean run is indistinguishable from a run whose fixture never reached the anonymiser at all. That pairing is a judgement about whether the fixture was representative, which is why it is a person's gate and not a machine's.
